task_read: A long-horizon ML post-training task: raise Llama-3.2-1B base from ~26% to ≥45% binary_strict on IFEval via the remote Tinker API, under a hard time/compute budget (timer.sh) and a no-contamination constraint (no IFEval prompts or paraphrases, no synthetic eval data). Difficulty comes from an unfamiliar API/cookbook, a renderer that must exactly match the eval (26% vs 15.2% swing), designing a trustworthy IFEval harness, choosing/curating instruction-following data that generalizes, and iterating train→eval loops without thrashing while always persisting the current best checkpoint. Warrants heavy, sustained meta-work across all five spine faculties.

dimensions.name: Tinker/cookbook, renderer & IFEval orientation
dimensions.description: Understanding the Tinker API + tinker_cookbook surface, the exact chat renderer that reproduces the ~26% baseline, what IFEval binary_strict actually measures, and the available (non-contaminating) training data before committing compute.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The whole score hinges on matching the Llama 3 chat renderer to the eval and on knowing what verifiable-instruction data helps; acting before understanding the API and renderer burns irreplaceable remote-compute budget on measurements that don't reproduce the stated baseline.

anchors.0: Jumps straight into a training call with no inspection of tinker_cookbook, renderer options, or IFEval scoring; treats the environment as a black box.
anchors.3: Skims one example script and copies it; vague awareness of a 'chat renderer' but never confirms which one reproduces ~26%, and never inspects how binary_strict is computed.
anchors.5: Reads the relevant cookbook/API pieces, identifies the Llama 3 chat renderer and a plausible instruction dataset, and understands binary_strict at a working level before training.
anchors.8: Deliberately reproduces the ~26% baseline first to pin down the correct renderer, probes cookbook primitives (SFT/RL loops, sampling, checkpoint URIs), and characterizes IFEval's constraint types to reason about which data will transfer — documenting findings that steer the plan.
anchors.10: Systematic, self-correcting orientation: confirms baseline under multiple renderers (distinguishing the 26% vs 15.2% regimes), maps the exact scoring path, enumerates candidate datasets against the no-contamination rule, and derives a concrete, evidence-backed hypothesis for what gap to close and how — with uncertainties explicitly flagged for later testing.

dimensions.name: Pipeline decomposition & milestone structure
dimensions.description: Breaking the effort into ordered sub-goals — reproduce baseline eval, stand up a training run, checkpoint+eval loop, iterate to target — each with an explicit done-check, rather than one undifferentiated 'train a model' push.
dimensions.why_it_matters: A remote train→checkpoint→eval loop has real latency and cost; sequencing it into checkpointed milestones with clear success criteria prevents wasted end-to-end attempts and makes the 45% target reachable within the time box.

anchors.0: No structure; a single monolithic attempt with no intermediate checkpoints or defined success criteria.
anchors.3: Implicit ordering only ('train then eval'); no explicit milestone gates or per-step done-conditions.
anchors.5: Clear ordered stages (baseline eval → first training run → eval → iterate) with a stated target per stage.
anchors.8: Milestones are explicit and each has a concrete pass/fail check (baseline reproduces ~26%; first run beats base; each iteration must exceed prior best), with early cheap milestones de-risking expensive ones and a decision rule for when to stop tuning.
anchors.10: A crisp, budget-aware milestone hierarchy that front-loads the cheapest highest-information checks, defines quantitative gates and expected score deltas per milestone, and sequences experiments so each result informs the next — visibly kept current as the run progresses.

dimensions.name: IFEval harness & score-trust design
dimensions.description: Deliberately building a trustworthy way to measure binary_strict on IFEval (correct renderer, correct scoring, enough samples) and confirming a claimed checkpoint truly hits the number — beyond just trusting a training loss curve.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The deliverable is defined entirely by a measured eval score; a renderer mismatch or a mis-wired scorer can make the agent chase a phantom improvement or under-report a real one, and a checkpoint written to the file without a trusted eval may not actually clear 45%.

anchors.0: Never measures IFEval independently; relies on training loss or a single unchecked number, or writes a checkpoint URI it never evaluated.
anchors.3: Runs some eval but with unverified renderer/scoring; treats a noisy one-off number as ground truth with no baseline sanity-check.
anchors.5: Has a working IFEval eval that reproduces the ~26% baseline, and re-evaluates candidate checkpoints on it before claiming an improvement.
anchors.8: Eval harness is validated against the known baseline, uses the eval renderer consistent with training, accounts for sampling noise (adequate sample size / determinism), and gates every 'new best' on a real re-measured score — plus guards against overfitting the metric given the no-contamination rule.
anchors.10: Rigorous, self-auditing verification: baseline reproduced and cross-checked, sampling variance quantified so improvements are distinguished from noise, held-out/generalization checks used to ensure gains aren't renderer or data artifacts, and every checkpoint written to best_checkpoint.txt is backed by a reproducible, trusted measurement of the exact reported metric.

dimensions.name: Budget-aware progress & best-so-far tracking
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of best-score-so-far vs the 45% target and remaining time (via timer.sh), and detecting when runs are plateauing, regressing, or thrashing.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Compute/time is bounded and remote; without tracking best-so-far against target and time left, the agent can over-invest in a dead-end approach or run out of budget with an un-persisted or sub-target result.

anchors.0: No tracking of scores across runs or time remaining; never consults the timer; loses track of which checkpoint is best.
anchors.3: Occasionally notes a score but no running comparison to target or budget; timer ignored until too late.
anchors.5: Keeps a clear record of each run's score vs the 45% target and checks remaining time periodically to inform effort.
anchors.8: Maintains an explicit ledger of experiments (config → score), always knows the current best and gap-to-target, checks timer.sh at decision points, and flags plateaus/regressions instead of repeating them.
anchors.10: Continuous, calibrated situational awareness: quantifies marginal score gain per unit budget, projects whether the current trajectory reaches 45% in the time left, recognizes diminishing returns or circular tuning early, and reallocates effort accordingly — never surprised by the clock.

dimensions.name: Approach revision on evidence
dimensions.description: Revising data mix, method (SFT vs RL), hyperparameters, or renderer when eval evidence shows the current approach isn't moving toward 45%, rather than repeating a falsified recipe.
dimensions.why_it_matters: First-choice data or hyperparameters rarely clear a +19-point gain on the first try; the agent must diagnose why a run underperformed and change the right lever, not grind the same config.

anchors.0: Repeats essentially the same run/config regardless of results; ignores disconfirming eval scores.
anchors.3: Makes random or superstitious changes after a poor result without diagnosing cause; changes many things at once so nothing is learned.
anchors.5: Responds to a weak eval by adjusting a plausible lever (data, LR, epochs) and re-testing, with a basic rationale.
anchors.8: Diagnoses the likely cause of underperformance (e.g., renderer mismatch, wrong data, under/over-training) and makes targeted, one-variable-informed changes, abandoning approaches shown not to transfer.
anchors.10: Treats each run as an experiment: forms hypotheses, changes levers deliberately to isolate effects, updates its mental model of what drives IFEval gains, and pivots decisively (including switching method) when evidence falsifies the current path — while preserving prior best results.

dimensions.name: Best-checkpoint persistence discipline
dimensions.description: Keeping /app/best_checkpoint.txt continuously updated with a valid Tinker sampler-checkpoint URI for the true best-so-far, so a timeout or crash never zeroes an achieved score.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The task explicitly requires immediately persisting each new best in the exact URI format; a great model that is never written (or written in the wrong format, or not updated when surpassed) yields no credit under the hard deadline.

anchors.0: Never writes best_checkpoint.txt, or writes a malformed/non-sampler URI.
anchors.3: Writes the file once late in the run; not kept in sync with the actual best; format not verified.
anchors.5: Writes a correctly-formatted sampler-checkpoint URI for a genuinely good checkpoint and updates it when clearly beaten.
anchors.8: Updates the file promptly on each verified new best in the exact required format, treating persistence as a first-class step so the deliverable is always valid mid-run.
anchors.10: Disciplined, defensive persistence: every verified best is written immediately in the correct URI form, the write is confirmed, stale/worse URIs are never left in place, and the file always reflects the true best even across interruptions near the deadline.
